newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-AUSTRALIAN BUSINESS NEWS - AUGUST 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The stockmarket yesterday slashed A$1 billion off the market capitalisation of BHP Co Ltd, a signal of mounting concerns with the company's handling of its global assets. Leading funds managers called for a shake-up in the top management of the company, while institutional investors called for the appointment of a independent chairman and new executives. Page 1.

Despite a large increase in revenue, the AMP Society expects to record a flat profit of about A$2 billion in 1997. Managing director and chief executive George Trumball said yesterday the company decided against disclosing its profit for the first half as it did not want to mislead its two million members in the lead up to November's vote on the proposed demutualisation. Page 33.

Better than expected earnings from Brambles Industries Ltd's United Kingdom based Chep pallet joint venture saw shares in the transport giant lift 5 per cent, or A$1.12 a share, to A$29.10. The result has led to a reworking of profit forecasts by analysts, who are lifting estimates up to around A$240 million from A$215 million. Page 33.

Group sales in Coles Myer for the three months to the end of July rose 6 per cent to A$4.72 billion, and full-year sales were up 5.8 per cent to A$19.22 billion. The solid figures allow Coles Myer to remain confident of achieving second-half profit growth of more than 20 per cent. Page 33.

Camerlin Group of Companies yesterday sold its entire 9.2 per cent stake in National Foods Ltd yesterday, and made a A$14.4 million profit on its A$35 million investment. The shares were sold on the market through BZW Australia at A$1.95 a share, up from the average of A$1.38 a share it paid last year. Page 33.

Rising European markets and Japanese stock improvements have assisted Kerr Neilson's Platinum Capital Ltd to improve strongly on its disappointing first half. Second half results showed a 16 percent rise in the net asset value per share, and the companyhas declared a dividend of 3 cents per share. Page 34.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A strong first half performance by the AMP Society saw total assets pass the A$100 million mark for the first time, and placed it in a favourable position in the lead up to its A$12 billion sharemarket listing. Managing director George Trumball said the figures placed the insurer on track to match last year's A$2.1 billion profit. Page 21.

Shares in Australia's largest company BHP dropped to A$17.44 yesterday following the second resignation of a senior company executive this week. Investors have not looked on the resignations, which followed a blow out in costs at BHP's A$1.65 billion hot briquetted iron (HBI) plant in Western Australia, favourably. Page 21.

The Australian Institute of Company Directors, headed by Foster's chairman John Ralph, yesterday called for a new two-tiered personal tax system that would include a rebate for low income earners. The AICD's call comes after Tuesday's High Court decision disallowing the States from collecting taxes on petrol, alcohol and tobacco. Page 21.

The wine industry is on target to exceed its 1997-98 forecasts after wine export sales broke through the A$600 million benchmark for the 12 months to July. Wine Export Council general manager Sam Tolley said the shipping figures of 156.9 litres worth A$68.3 million represented growth in the value and volume of shipments. Page 23.

The New South Wales Department of Urban Affairs and Planning says the proposed A$660 million Eastern distributor in Sydney, which is expected to begin construction next week, will reach capacity constraints at traffic levels lower than the volumes of trafic growth forecast in its prospectus. Page 23.

A delegation representing some of Australia's biggest businesses has warned the Federal Government that the Victorian Government could threaten national energy reforms as it moves to cream millions of dollars from electricity consumers through new taxes. age 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

While the AMP Society declined to release the profit figure for the six months to the end of June, it yesterday showed its place as Australia's financial powerhouse by passing A$100 billion of funds under management in the June half, setting the platform or a profit for 1997 of over A$2 billion. Page 25.

Earnings in the Ten Group lifted by 11 per cent to A$154.5 million in the first half of 1997 yesterday, as the company, which is anxiously awaiting a Federal Court decision that will decide when it can list on the stockmarket, predicted further strong groth. Page 25.

The departure of two BHP executives - minerals chief Dick Carter and iron ore group general manager Geoff Wedlock - led to investors wiping A$1 billion off BHP's sharemarket value yesterday. The departures relate to the blowout in costs of the company'snew HBI plant in Western Australia. Page 25.

Australian Shareholders' Association executive officer Tony McLean says the Association is concerned over the level of confusion related to the prospectus for Envestra, Boral's gas distribution spin-off. McLean said about two-thirds of Envestra's forecast distributions are repayments on principal initially contributed by investors. Page 27.

Allan Handberg, the chief executive of the Australian Chamber of Manufacturers will stand down from his demanding job after four years. Handberg has headed industry lobbying of the Government on issues such as tax reform and tariffs, and has briefed govenments and business on a wide spectrum of issues. Page 27.

Following recommendations outlined in the Wallis report, the Financial Planning Association and the Association of Financial Advisers have taken the first steps in merging, signing a memorandum of understanding which should provide an outline for a closerworking relationship. Page 27.
THE AGE

In a short statement, BHP chief executive John Prescott has announced BHP iron ore operations head Geoff Wedlock has resigned. The resignation comes as more than A$1 billion was wiped off the value of BHP stocks because of increasing concerns over the blwout in costs of the HBI plant in Western Australia's Pilbara. Page B1.

Despite a 15 per cent drop in contributions from its New Zealand businesses, Coles Myer reported a 6 per cent rise in final quarter sales to A$4.72 billion. The figures place the retailer on track to report a 23 per cent rise in full year profit, and sugest the overhaul of its retail brands has been a success. Page B1.

Optus Communications has, over the past few months, gained more than 10,000 customers in its bid to join the A$5 billion local call market, in which Telstra has traditionally held the monopoly. Optus' push into the local call market comes after it repaired the software meltdown which stalled last year's high-profile launch. Page B1.

Property investors are braced for at least three new property floats - Prudential Assurance's launch of a A$213 million property trust to fund the development of two projects in Sydney's CBD; Axion Funds Management's A$150 million raising for its Sydney idustrial portfolio; and Ord Minnett's A$450 million float of the Sundowner Hotel Trust. Page B1.

The ANZ Bank has linked up with credit card giant Visa International to trial Australia's first secure Internet commerce platform. The system, which gives ANZ an edge on its competitors, is based on the secure electronic transaction (SET) version 1.0 proocol released in early June. Page B3.

Official VFACTS registration figures released yesterday show a rise in car sales of 7 per cent for the 12 months to July compared with the corresponding period last year. The figures confirm industry expectations that sales this year will be the best sine 1985. Page B3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
